{{Use list-defined references|date=October 2020}}
'''Ineke Anežka Lucia Stoop''' (born 1953){{r|diss}} is a retired Dutch [[Survey methodology|survey statistician]] who was Head of Methodology at the {{ill|Netherlands Institute for Social Research|nl|Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau}} (SCB) and chaired the European Statistical Advisory Committee (ESAC).{{r|aapor}}

==Education and career==
Stoop was born on 14 March 1953 in [[The Hague]]. She earned a master's degree in psychology at [[Leiden University]] in 1980, and completed her Ph.D. in 2005 at [[Utrecht University]].{{r|diss|scb}}

She was a researcher at Leiden University from 1973 to 1983 before joining the Netherlands Institute for Social Research in 1983, and became Head of Methodology at the Institute in 1990.{{r|diss|scb}}

She became chair of the European Statistical Advisory Committee in 2014,{{r|eurostat}} and retired in 2019.{{r|aapor}}

==Books==
Stoop is the author of books including:
*''The Hunt for the Last Respondent: Nonresponse in Sample Surveys'' (her 2005 doctoral dissertation){{r|diss|hlr}}
*''Improving Survey Response: Lessons learned from the European Social Survey''{{r|isr}} (with Jaak Billiet, Achim Koch and Rory Fitzgerald, Wiley, 2010)

She is also the editor or co-editor of [[edited volume]]s including
*''Access Panels and Online Research, Panacea Or Pitfall?'' (Uitgeverij Aksant, 2008)
*''Advances on Comparative Survey Methodology'' (Wiley, 2018){{r|keynote}}

==Recognition==
Stoop is an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}} She was part of the [[European Social Survey]] project, which won the [[Descartes Prize]] in 2005.{{r|eurostat|descartes}} She was a keynote speaker at the 2019 biennial conference of the [[European Survey Research Association]], in [[Zagreb]],{{r|keynote}} where she was given the association's Outstanding Service Award.{{r|aapor|lifetime}}
